alt: Houses at whole-number positions along a road. A well is tried at each house in turn, with each house labeled by its walking distance and the left and right sums computed from prefix sums. A spot between two houses is shown to cost between its neighbors, so only house positions are checked, and the cheapest one is marked.

steps.caption: 5 houses stand along a road at the marked positions. A well goes at a whole-number spot, and the cost is the total walking distance from every house to it. Checking every spot costs a full pass over the houses each time, so look for a short list of spots to check.
Well at house 2. Left: 2 x 0 - 0 = 0. Right: 34 - 2 x 4 = 26. Total 26. New best: 26 at 2. Labels show each house's distance.
Well at house 3. Left: 3 x 1 - 2 = 1. Right: 31 - 3 x 3 = 22. Total 23. New best: 23 at 3. Labels show each house's distance.
Well at house 7. Left: 7 x 2 - 5 = 9. Right: 24 - 7 x 2 = 10. Total 19. New best: 19 at 7. Labels show each house's distance.
Well at house 9. Left: 9 x 3 - 12 = 15. Right: 15 - 9 x 1 = 6. Total 21. Best stays 19 at 7. Labels show each house's distance.
Well at house 15. Left: 15 x 4 - 21 = 39. Right: 0 - 15 x 0 = 0. Total 39. Best stays 19 at 7. Labels show each house's distance.

What about a spot between houses, like 4? Its cost is 22, between the neighbors' 23 and 19. Between two houses each step right adds the same amount, so the cost runs along a straight line and an end is never worse.
Only the 5 house positions need checking. The cheapest is 19 with the well at 7.
